lines: Here's the whole batch, baker. We didn't start out a little off. Paul says we were "dead in our trespasses" (Eph 2:5). We walked in the ways of this world and of the ruler of the power of the air, gave our flesh whatever it craved, and were by nature children of wrath (Eph 2:1-3).
And dead means DEAD, friend. A dead guy can't fix his life. He can't even hit the snooze button.

So the rescue had to be all God. Out of His rich mercy and great love, He made dead people alive with Christ, and we brought nothing to it but the need (Eph 2:4-5). Then He raised us up with Christ and seated us with Him in the heavenly realms, so that in the coming ages He might display the surpassing riches of His grace, shown in His kindness to us in Christ Jesus (Eph 2:6-7).
That's grace. Being saved is God's gift, received through faith, not a paycheck for our works, so nobody gets to brag (Eph 2:8-9).
Think about it. Nobody brags about how hard they worked to open a present.
And good works? They're not how we get saved. They're what God made us in Christ Jesus to do (Eph 2:10).
Grace first, works second. Flip that order and you're frosting the cookie before it's even baked. And Paul's not done with this letter yet, friend.
